meta.note: Educational comparison, not a prediction and not an official evacuation plan. A screening of where a second way out could go, not engineering, environmental review or legal analysis. Counts only: no parcel identifiers, owners, addresses or imagery are stored. Coordinates in local meters (network.json crs) and WGS84.
meta.crs: EPSG:32610 local: x = easting - xmin, y = northing - ymin (meters)

cost.note: Low: the FDOT flat-terrain urban two-lane figure; high: 3 times it for hillside retaining walls, grading and drainage (assumption). Fire roads and tracks start from the Cambria gravel-road figure. Steep links are priced at the length a 15% road would need. Acquisition: each building in the corridor taken whole at the block group median home value (± the ACS margin of error); each other parcel crossed is a partial take at 10–25% of that value (assumption). Relocation, engineering, environmental review and legal costs are left out.

grade15.what: Sonoma County fire-access bulletin: 15% maximum grade by default, steeper sections up to 20% only with Fire Chief approval (an example of a local standard)

grade20.what: State Minimum Fire Safe Regulations, 14 CCR §1273.03: road and driveway grades shall not exceed 16% at any point; up to 20% only with local approval and mitigation

fdot.what: Florida DOT Cost Per Mile Models, U01 "New Construction 2 Lane Undivided Urban Arterial with 4' Bike Lanes": $9,116,872.25 per mile (flat terrain, no right of way)
fdot.retrieved: 2026-11-01 (Wayback copy of 2025-10-06; the live page returned 404)

cambria.what: Civil Design Studio for the Cambria CSD, "Cambria Emergency Evacuation Route: Preliminary Cost Estimate", 2024-02-12: about $2.55M with 10% contingency for 12,000 ft of 16 ft gravel emergency road on an existing graded alignment

acs.what: American Community Survey 2020–2024 5-year, table B25077 median value of owner-occupied homes, by block group (via the Census Reporter API; the Census Bureau API now requires a key); block group from TIGERweb

parcels.what: Alameda County Parcel Boundaries (Parcels FeatureServer layer 0), geometry only; counted per candidate and never saved

osm.what: OpenStreetMap buildings, footways, paths, steps, tracks, parks and institutional land (Overpass API; © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL)

city.what: City of Berkeley "2nd Route Out" (Imagined_Road_Panoramic_Hill_Berkeley_WFL1, layer 0, "Imagined Road: Connects Dwight Way in Berkeley and Dwight Place in Oakland", "For Evacuation Time Study", edited 2025-06-27)

provenance.area: derived: area id in data/model/access-constraints.json (as the network stands)
provenance.type: model rule: new = straight segment between two network nodes; path = existing path, stairway or no-vehicle segment widened; barrier = diverter, bollard or gate opened; city = the City's "2nd Route Out" snapped to network nodes
provenance.geom: derived: candidate geometry from tools/egress-candidates.mjs (straight line between two network nodes, an existing path, or the City concept snapped to nodes); not a design
provenance.profile: derived: ground elevation every ~4 m from the 4 m lidar DEM; avg = end-to-end climb / length; p90 and max = 25 m windows (p90 as the network builder's gradeMax)
provenance.gradeFlags: model rule: over15 / over20 when the average or the 90th-percentile 25 m window exceeds 15% (a common local fire-access limit; Sonoma County example) or 20% (the ceiling in 14 CCR §1273.03 with approval)
provenance.lengthAt15PctM: derived: length a road would need to keep a 15% grade over the same climb (switchbacks); not a design
provenance.pathShare: derived: share of the line within 6 m of an OpenStreetMap footway, path, steps, track or a network path/no-vehicle segment
provenance.buildingsInCorridor: derived: OpenStreetMap building footprints touching a 12.2 m corridor centered on the line (assumption: corridor width); counts only
provenance.parcels: derived: Alameda County parcel polygons (geometry only, not stored) crossed by the centerline for 2 m or more (crossed), touching the corridor (inCorridor), and the share of the centerline outside every parcel (public right of way or unparceled land); null where the County layer has no parcels (Contra Costa County)
provenance.followsRightOfWay: derived: 90% or more of the centerline lies outside parcels
provenance.land: derived: share of the line inside OpenStreetMap park or nature-reserve or protected-area polygons, UC, LBNL or East Bay Regional Park District land (by name, operator or owner tags); outer rings only
provenance.fireZone: sourced (City Fire Zones) at the midpoint, or the simulator's 90 m elevation proxy outside Berkeley
provenance.drivingNowM: derived: drivable distance between the two endpoints today (undirected)
provenance.access: derived: tools/access-constraints.mjs rerun with the link added (two-way local street, 20 ft, no residents on it): residents no longer behind any choke, and the target area's residents still behind one, its nesting and the chokes that remain
provenance.cost: assumption: screening ranges from public figures (meta.cost, meta.sources); not an engineer's estimate
provenance.evacuation: derived from synthetic runs: tools/egress-sim.mjs, same seed with and without the link
